issues.display_title: Issue #424: Editor: a recoloured shape's outline should follow its fill
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Editor 2D canvas — follow-up to #407.

Description

Recolouring a shape changes only its fill. The outline stays the default orange, so a shape filled teal is drawn with an orange edge that has nothing to do with it.

The outline should follow the fill — the same colour, darker or lighter, so the edge still reads.

Root cause

The fill honours the per-shape colour; the stroke never does (draw.ts:253-254):

c2.fillStyle = sh.color ?? C.shapeFill; c2.fill();
c2.lineWidth = px(isSel ? 2 : 1.25); c2.strokeStyle = C.shapeStroke; c2.stroke();

C.shapeStroke is the fixed #FA9E3D from #407. It pairs with the default fill #EFD3C8 and looks right there, but it is applied to every shape regardless of what the user picked.

Scope

  • Derive the outline from the shape's own colour when one is set: shift it away from its own lightness — darker for a light fill, lighter for a dark one — so the edge stays visible either way.
  • A shape with no explicit colour keeps C.shapeStroke. #FA9E3D / #EFD3C8 is a design pair from #407, not a computed shade, and it should stay exactly as approved.
  • sh.color comes from an <input type="color"> (SelectionToolbars.tsx:279) so it is always #rrggbb, but the helper should also cope with the rgb()/rgba() form the palette tokens use.
  • The in-progress shape draft keeps the default stroke — it has no colour yet.

Not in scope

  • Resize handles and the group bounding box keep C.shapeStroke. They are selection chrome, not part of the shape; tinting them per shape would make them harder to spot against their own fill.
  • 3D and the map need nothing. Neither draws a shape outline — the map's shapeFill layer sets fill-color only, with no fill-outline-color (layer-definitions.ts:92-99), and the 3D shape is a solid mesh.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Recolouring a shape changes its outline to a matching darker/lighter version of the new fill.
  • A light fill gets a darker outline; a dark fill gets a lighter one.
  • A shape with no explicit colour is unchanged from #407 — #EFD3C8 fill, #FA9E3D outline.
  • Selected and unselected shapes both follow this; only the stroke width still differs.
  • Resize handles and the group bounding box are unchanged.
  • Unit tests for the outline derivation (light fill, dark fill, hex short/long form, rgb()/rgba() input, unparsable input).
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

A shape with its own colour now derives its outline from it, via the new outlineFor() in editor/palette.ts. A shape without one keeps C.shapeStroke — #FA9E3D / #EFD3C8 is a design pair from #407, not a computed shade, so the default look is untouched.

The lightness threshold is 0.25, not 0.5

The obvious rule — lighten below 0.5, darken above — is wrong here, and the test caught it before merge. The outline sits on the boundary between the fill and the pale canvas, so a lighter edge disappears into the background for anything but a genuinely dark fill. The reported teal #1E92AE has a Rec. 601 luminance of 0.45: under a 0.5 threshold it would have been lightened, which is exactly the wrong direction.

Darkening is the readable default; lightening is the escape hatch for fills with no room left to darken.

Details

  • outlineFor parses short hex, long hex and rgb()/rgba() — the picker is an <input type="color"> so it always sends hex, but the palette's own tokens are rgba. An unparsable colour is returned untouched rather than guessed at.
  • Resize handles and the group bounding box keep C.shapeStroke, as scoped: they are selection chrome, not part of the shape.
  • 3D and the map needed nothing — neither draws a shape outline.

Files

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/palette.ts — outlineFor(), rgbOf()

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts — shape stroke

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/palette.test.ts — 7 new tests

  • Branch: feature/424-shape-outline-from-fill · Commit: b434ffd · PR #425

  • pnpm test (533 passing), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green. The 2 suite failures (renameSweep.test.ts, api/upload/route.test.ts EACCES on /tmp) pre-date this branch and are unrelated.

issues.display_title: Issue #431: Clear wizard persistence when entering editor via "Continue to Editor" (step 4)
issues.main_description_html:
Fixes feedback bug #429.

Description

After a project is created, the wizard should immediately clear its persisted step-by-step data. Today that only happens on ONE of the two ways out of step 4:

  • Generate Project → editor: useWizardPersistence observes the generatedTwin transition and runs the completion latch — updateProject(..., { status: "scanned", isComplete: true }) + localStorage.removeItem(storageKey()) (src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts:266-276).
  • Continue to Editor (no generate): enterEditor in src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx:80-94 routes straight to /editor (blank canvas path, or openInEditor for a restored twin) without touching persistence. The wizard blob stays in localStorage and the project is never marked isComplete, so the next /start restores the stale wizard at step 4.

Note the persistence hook cannot observe this path by subscription — enterEditor does not change generatedTwin (a twin restored from persistence is already set on mount, so the !prev.generatedTwin && state.generatedTwin transition never fires). The clear has to happen where the wizard is exited.

Suggested fix

Run the same completion latch on the enterEditor path: clear the wizard localStorage blob (storageKey(projectId)) and updateProject(projectId, { isComplete: true }) before router.push("/editor"). Prefer one shared "complete wizard" helper both exits route through, rather than duplicating the latch.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Step 4 "Continue to Editor" (without generating) clears the persisted wizard data and sets the project isComplete: true
  • "Continue to Editor" after a generated/loaded twin (Open Editor) also leaves no stale wizard persistence
  • Existing generate path behavior unchanged (status: "scanned", isComplete: true, blob cleared)
  • After entering the editor, visiting /start begins a fresh wizard instead of restoring the old one
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Muhamad Rifky — Developer

RESULT

Both exits out of wizard step 4 now route through one shared completion latch.

New: src/lib/wizard/completeWizard.ts — completeWizard(projectId, fields?) removes the wizard blob (storageKey(), the unkeyed wizard-context key) and calls updateProject(projectId, { ...fields, isComplete: true }).

Changed:

  • src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts:266 — generate path calls the helper with { generatedTwin, status: "scanned" }; behavior unchanged. Keeps the wizardComplete ref latch, needed because the wizard stays mounted after generating and the autosave subscriber would otherwise rewrite the blob just removed.
  • src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx:80 — enterEditor calls completeWizard on both branches (restored twin → openInEditor, and blank canvas → floorConfigs merged into the same update call). Called last, after each branch's store writes, for the same autosave reason.
  • src/lib/wizard/__tests__/completeWizard.test.ts — 3 cases (blob dropped + isComplete, caller fields preserved, no-project-id still clears).

Second defect found and fixed: bare /editor resolves the project from localStorage.gf_project_id, which the wizard never writes for a draft (setWizardProjectId skips it, and /start freshStart deletes it). "Continue to Editor" therefore pushed /editor → no id → redirect back to /start. The stale blob used to restore step 4 and mask it; with the blob correctly cleared it would have landed on a blank step 1. Both exits now push /editor/<projectId> (src/hooks/useDigitalTwinExport.ts:57, src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx:95).

Verification: pnpm lint clean, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean for this change, pnpm test 546 passed. Two test files (mappedin-editor/convert, api/upload/route) and three tsc errors (@testing-library/react, .next route validator) fail identically on the unmodified branch — pre-existing, not caused by this change. Not covered: no jsdom test of the React exit path; jsdom/@testing-library/react are not installed in this repo (three existing render tests already fail on that).

Commit: 663f24f

issues.display_title: Issue #432: Mappedin import: locations/objects not imported into project, silent create failure
issues.main_description_html:
Fixes feedback bug #428. Sample Mappedin zip for reproduction will be attached by the reporter/assignee.

Description

Importing a Mappedin file detects data and shows it in the import summary, but the resulting project is incomplete:

  1. Information (locations) not imported — detected and counted in the summary modal, but absent from the created project.
  2. Objects not imported — door, window, circle, rectangle, polygon, point, safety annotation are missing after import. attachObjectCounts (src/lib/mappedin-import/attachObjectCounts.ts) counts points/shapes/safetyAnnotations off the parsed levels, so the summary can show them even if the staging path only carries walls/areas into the project.
  3. Silent create failure — creating a new project from the import can fail with no error message about the failed tour creation. Audit the create/updateProject chain in the import flow for swallowed rejections (.catch(() => {}) pattern) and surface an error toast/state.

Code areas: src/lib/mappedin-import/ (runImport.ts, extractLocations.ts, attachObjectCounts.ts), src/components/setup/import-mappedin/, staging/navigation in StepUploadFloor.

Repro with the sample zip first to pin which of the three are one root cause (staging drops non-wall/area data) vs separate bugs.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Detected locations/information end up in the imported project
  • Detected objects (door, window, circle, rectangle, polygon, point, safety annotation) end up in the imported project
  • Failed project/tour creation during import shows a visible error message
  • Import summary counts match what actually lands in the project
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Root cause: the Mappedin converter only handled kinds wall + room/hallway; object, poi, safety annotations, doors (which live in connections.json, not kinds) and locations.json were parsed or counted but never staged. A silently-failed createProject (swallowed in useWizardPersistence) additionally bounced /editor back to /start with no message.

Fixed (branch feature/432-mappedin-import-objects):

  • src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts + parse.ts + types.ts: polygon object kinds → polygon shapes; poi points → point annotations; annotations/<floor>.json → safety annotations (heart-defibrillator→aed); connections.json type:"door" → floorplanMeta.doors segments (swing "none" — Mappedin carries no swing data); locations.json → project-wide Information records (name/description/icon/photos) with infoId links on anchored areas/shapes/points. Rotate/translate/bbox transforms now cover all imported object kinds.
  • src/lib/mappedin-import/detectSource.ts: passes informationRecords through; attachObjectCounts.ts counts doors/windows so the summary matches what lands.
  • src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx: stages Information records on Continue/Add More Floors; creates the project at Continue when the wizard's own create was skipped/failed and shows an error instead of navigating silently.

Verified against both sample zips:

  • Sample 1 (airport, 2 floors): 24 shapes, 23 pois, 2 AED safety annotations, 57 doors (49+8), 35 Information records, 34+ linked.
  • Sample 2 (school, 1 floor): 96 shapes, 1 poi, 44 doors, 65 Information records, 67 linked.
  • Windows: neither export carries window data — nothing to import.
  • Stairs/elevator connections skipped by design (their spaces already import as areas).

pnpm test (557 passed), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green. Integration test src/lib/mappedin/__tests__/sample-zip.int.test.ts auto-skips when the sample zip is absent.

Commits: 4923f3e, 8efc532

issues.display_title: Issue #436: Mappedin import: project is_complete never set true after Continue to Editor
issues.main_description_html:
Follow-up of #432 / feedback #428. Related to #431 (same latch, step-4 generate path — assigned separately).

Description

Completing a Mappedin import ("Continue to Editor" in StepUploadFloor) leaves the project with is_complete: false. The completion latch lives in useWizardPersistence and only fires on the generatedTwin transition (src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts:266-276) — the import path never sets generatedTwin, so updateProject(..., { isComplete: true }) never runs and the wizard blob is never cleared.

Consequence: the project stays "incomplete" in the dashboard/API, and revisiting /start restores a stale wizard instead of treating the project as done.

Suggested fix

In handleContinueToEditor (src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx), after the project is ensured: updateProject(projectId, { isComplete: true }) and clear the wizard persistence blob, mirroring the generate-path latch.

Acceptance Criteria

  • After Mappedin import → Continue to Editor, the project has is_complete: true
  • Wizard persistence for that project is cleared (fresh /start afterwards)
  • Generate path behavior unchanged
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Root cause confirmed: the isComplete latch in useWizardPersistence only fires on the generatedTwin transition, which the Mappedin import path never takes. Fixed by routing the import's Continue to Editor through the shared completeWizard() latch from #431 (sets isComplete: true and drops the wizard autosave blob), called in handleContinueToEditor after the project is ensured and the store writes land, before navigation.

Files: src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx (+5 lines).
pnpm test (560 passed), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #369: Verify Mappedin import assumptions against real sample files
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

The Mappedin import extractors carry four TODO(repo) assumptions that were never verified against real-world samples (extractFloors.ts, extractLocations.ts):

  • floor stack order is assumed ground-first — a reversed sample would import upside-down
  • floor names are not truncated to MapThru's real name max (unknown)
  • heights assume metres — a sample in feet/map units would import wrong scale
  • location records map only basic fields; richer Mappedin fields (categories, links) are dropped

Scope

  • Collect 2–3 real Mappedin export samples (single + multi-floor)
  • Verify/fix stack order, add name truncation once the max is known, add unit conversion if needed, map richer location fields where MapThru has a target field
  • Remove the four TODO markers

Acceptance Criteria

  • Import verified against real samples with correct order, scale, and names
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

All four TODO(#369) assumptions verified against two real Mappedin exports (airport 2-floor, school 1-floor) and resolved:

  1. Floor stack order — real bug found and fixed. Mappedin lists floor-stacks top-first, while the app's contract is canvasData.levels bottom→top (levelBaseHeights, levelsAtOrBelow). The parser now reverses the stack (and the floors.geojson fallback) to ground-first. Note for the future: floors.geojson elevation is an entry-floor ordinal (airport's "Level 2" carries 0, "Level 1" carries −1), NOT a physical height — never use it as a sort key. Floor names import verbatim from the export (the airport demo genuinely names its busy entry concourse "Level 2"); the import summary lists floors bottom-up by design.
  2. Heights are metres — verified on both samples (maxHeight 3–4 m); existing clamp unchanged.
  3. Name truncation — dropped the TODO; longest real name is 29 chars, no observed limit to enforce.
  4. Richer location fields — links → Information.hyperlinks (URLs through withScheme, url-less links dropped), location-categories.json → project-wide Category records staged with the import, location categories → Information.categoryIds.

All four TODO(#369) markers removed. Files: src/lib/mappedin/{parse,convert,types}.ts, src/lib/mappedin-import/{detectSource,extractFloors,extractLocations}.ts, src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx, tests + real-sample integration test.

pnpm test (561 passed), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green. Verified in-app against the airport sample (sequence badges ground-first, pairing correct).

Commits: 1474ecd, 591b246, 2c3084f

issues.display_title: Issue #438: Edit Information modal: object label style dropdown not working
issues.main_description_html:
Fixes feedback bug #437.

Description

In the Edit Information modal, the "Object label style" dropdown isn't working — it should offer/display the label style options (text, icon, logo, photo/banner) in the dropdown menu, and the chosen style should apply to the object's label on the map.

Code: the dropdown lives in src/components/editor/information-modal/MediaTab.tsx (labelType Select over LABEL_TYPES, plus per-type pickers for icon/logo/photo; Information.labelType drives label rendering per useMapStore.types). Repro against the reporter's screenshot to pin which part fails:

  • dropdown doesn't open / renders empty (shadcn Select portal/z-index inside the modal is a known suspect), or
  • options render but the selection doesn't persist to the Information record, or
  • selection persists but the map label doesn't re-render per labelType (text/icon/logo/photo).

Acceptance Criteria

  • "Object label style" dropdown opens inside the Edit Information modal and lists all styles (text, icon, logo, photo)
  • Selecting a style persists on the Information record and survives reopening the modal
  • The map label renders according to the chosen style (icon picker / logo / photo choices respected)
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Two changes shipped:

  1. Root cause of the dead dropdown (#437): the Edit Information modal overlay sits at z-60 while the shadcn Select positioner defaults to z-50 — the open list rendered behind the modal. Fixed with the documented positionerClassName="z-[70]" override on both Selects inside the modal (label style in MediaTab, social platform in ContactTab); repo swept for other modals with the same bug — none left.

  2. Label style options + validation (follow-up request): dropdown options renamed to Text / Icon / Logo / Photo and a new Pano style added (ObjectLabelType/Information.labelType + resolveLabelRender renders the linked panorama's thumbnail chip). Choosing Logo/Photo/Pano without their asset now shows a red validation message under the dropdown and blocks Save — one shared labelAssetError() drives both the inline message and validate(). Icon keeps its graceful text fallback (its picker sits right below).

Files: src/lib/map/objectLabel.ts, src/store/useMapStore.types.ts, src/components/editor/information-modal/{MediaTab,ContactTab,shared}.ts(x), src/lib/map/__tests__/objectLabel.test.ts.

Select an area row, then click a door (or wall/window) row in the sidebar object list: the area stays selected, so both the area and the door end up highlighted at once. issues.display_title: Issue #446: Editor save downgrades a published project to draft
issues.main_description_html:
The dashboard's "Published" status flips to "Draft" after editing a project. Every editor save (manual and autosave) sends updateProject(id, { canvasData, status: "edited" }) unconditionally (EditorTopbar.saveNow), overwriting a published status; the dashboard shows anything ≠ published as "Draft".

Fix

  • Keep the project's status in the map store when the editor loads the project (useWizardPersistence — the single project-load path).
  • In saveNow, only send status: "edited" when the current status is not published.

Acceptance criteria

  • Saving/autosaving a published project keeps it "Published" on the dashboard.
  • Saving a non-published project still moves it to edited.
  • BE counterpart guards the transition server-side (see BE task).

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Parent feedback: #439

RESULT

Root cause: EditorTopbar.saveNow sent status: "edited" on every save (manual + autosave), downgrading a published project; the dashboard shows anything ≠ published as "Draft".

Fix: the map store now keeps the backend project status (projectStatus in projectSlice), set where the editor loads the project payload (useWizardPersistence). saveNow omits the status field when the current status is published — publish state only changes via the publish/unpublish endpoints. Non-published projects still move to edited on save.

BE counterpart: Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#119 guards the same transition server-side.

Files: src/components/editor/EditorTopbar.tsx, src/store/mapStore/projectSlice.ts, src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts

issues.display_title: Issue #454: Empty project: .txt import leaves the No-floors card and never saves
issues.main_description_html:
Repro

  1. Open an empty project (no floors) in the editor.
  2. Import a floorplan .txt via the "No floors yet" card's dropzone (drop or browse), e.g. the edited_floorplan (4).txt attached to #439.
  3. The walls render on the canvas (and in the 3D view), but:
    • the "No floors yet" card stays on top of the canvas, and
    • nothing is ever saved — reloading the project shows an empty project again.

Cause
EmptyProjectPlaceholder.loadTxt only calls engine.loadText(text, name). The model lands in the floorplan engine, but no floor is created in the store: floorConfigs and canvasData.levels stay empty, so

  • hasFloors(floorConfigs, canvasData) stays false → EditorCanvas keeps rendering the placeholder, and
  • the engine→store sync has no level to write into, so autosave persists nothing.

Fix direction
Importing a .txt on an empty project must first create a floor (floor config + canvasData level, same as Add Floor), then load the model into it — so the placeholder hides and the engine sync/autosave has a level target.

Acceptance criteria

  • Importing a .txt on an empty project hides the "No floors yet" card and shows the imported floorplan.
  • A floor exists afterwards (floor list shows it) and the project autosaves — reload shows the imported floorplan.
  • Add Floor flow unchanged.

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Parent feedback: #439 (attachment file)

RESULT

Root cause confirmed as scoped: EmptyProjectPlaceholder.loadTxt called engine.loadText only — the model landed in the engine, but no floor existed in the store, so hasFloors() stayed false (card stayed up) and the engine→store sync had no level to persist (no autosave).

Fix: the dropzone now goes through the store instead of the engine — parse via the existing txtToLevel, add a floor config (Floor N, height 3, originalFileName = the imported file), append the level to canvasData (adopting computeCoordSpace when the project had none) and set it active. FloorplanEditor's level-load effect then loads the model into the engine, the card unmounts (hasFloors true), and setCanvasData marks unsaved so autosave persists it. A malformed .txt shows a red error line under the dropzone instead of silently doing nothing.

Files: src/components/editor/EmptyProjectPlaceholder.tsx
Branch: feature/454-txt-import-empty-project
Commit: 95aa664

Repro
Add Floor modal → Import → pick a MapThru floorplan .txt export (e.g. edited_floorplan (5).txt attached to #447) → red error: invalid editor export JSON: invalid character '2' after top-level value.

Cause
useAddLevel.handleImport sends every .txt/.json to /api/import/mappedin-editor, which parses a Mappedin editor export (JSON). A MapThru floorplan .txt is the engine's own plain-number format (W H / wall count / coordinate lines) — the Go JSON decoder reads the first number as a top-level value and fails on the second.

Fix

  • Sniff the file content in handleImport: if it does not start with {/[, treat it as a MapThru floorplan .txt and convert locally via txtToLevel (modal name + height apply) — same path the empty-project dropzone uses since #454. JSON still goes to /api/import/mappedin-editor, .zip to /api/import/mappedin.
  • Extract the shared "append floorplan txt as a new floor" logic (floor config + level + coordSpace + active level) into lib/editor/levels.ts and reuse it from both the dropzone and the modal.

Acceptance criteria

  • Importing a MapThru floorplan .txt from the Add Floor modal creates the floor and shows it (no BE call, no error).
  • A malformed .txt shows the modal's error state.
  • Mappedin editor JSON and .zip imports unchanged.

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Parent feedback: #447

RESULT

handleImport now sniffs the file content before choosing a route: a .txt that does not start with {/[ is a MapThru floorplan export (plain numbers) and is converted locally via the new appendTxtLevel helper — floor config uses the modal's name + height, the level is appended with a computed coordSpace when the building had none, and the floor becomes active. Mappedin editor JSON still goes to /api/import/mappedin-editor and .zip to /api/import/mappedin; no BE change. A malformed .txt shows the modal's error state instead of the Go JSON error.

Shared logic extracted to lib/editor/levels.ts (isFloorplanTxt + appendTxtLevel) and the empty-project dropzone (#454) now reuses it. 5 unit tests added (format sniffing, parse/append/coordSpace, throw on non-floorplan text).

issues.display_title: Issue #450: Create Empty Project modal: details form, autocomplete, lat/lng validation, drop pin
issues.main_description_html:
PRD #427 — Create Empty Project (part 2 of 3).

Description

Modal for creating a project without a floor plan image:

  • Project Name — required.
  • Address / Label — optional, with autocomplete.
  • Latitude / Longitude — validated (-90..90 / -180..180), typing valid coordinates moves the map/pin.
  • Map with drop pin — dropping a pin updates coordinates and address/label when available.

Reuse the wizard location pieces (src/components/setup/StepSelectLocation.tsx, MapAddressOverlay.tsx) and the existing createProject server action (src/actions/projects.ts) — the API already accepts name/address/lat/lng without an image. On success route directly to /editor/<projectId>.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Project Name is required before creation
  • Address / Label is optional and supports autocomplete
  • Latitude must be between -90 and 90; Longitude between -180 and 180
  • Dropping a pin updates coordinates and address/label when available
  • Typing valid coordinates moves the map/pin
  • Confirm is disabled until required fields are valid
  • Confirm cannot be submitted twice while creating
  • Creation failure keeps the modal open and preserves entered data
  • Successful creation opens the editor directly
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green
